name: Claude Code

surfaces.label: Claude Code extension for VS Code and forks

working_signals.name: caffeinate
working_signals.meaning: Claude Code holds an idle-sleep inhibitor for exactly the length of a turn

waiting_signals.meaning: needs permission or has been idle waiting for input

sources.evidence: strings in ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.283: 'caffeinate' '-i' '-t' 'Started ... to prevent sleep' 'Stopped sleep inhibitor, allowing sleep'; ps shows caffeinate as a child of the busy sessions only

sources.claim: 2 of 10 sessions working, 8 idle, separated by caffeinate child and CPU (9-11% vs under 1%)
sources.evidence: per-session table from ps/pgrep on the maintainer's Mac

sources.claim: transcripts are JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl with 30-day cleanup

the extension's native binary lives under ~/.vscode/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-*/ and would otherwise be labelled a terminal session; ~/.local/bin/claude as a path prefix also matched claude-swap
sources.evidence: completeness critic of the research storm, run against tools/agents_probe.py matches() on this Mac; ls ~/.local/bin shows claude-swap

sources.claim: the desktop app's --bg-pty-host launcher is not a session (its child is); claude mcp, daemon, doctor, update and --version are not sessions
sources.evidence: ps on this Mac: pid 81300 .../ClaudeCode.app/Contents/MacOS/claude --bg-pty-host <socket>, child 81331 on ttys009 is the session; completeness critic of wave 2 ran tools/agents_probe.py matches() on each command line

notes: Sessions that share a working directory share a project folder, so map a process to its transcript by session id, never by folder. The desktop app runs sessions as child processes of a launcher at ClaudeCode.app/Contents/MacOS/claude. Matching reads the command line only: Claude Code runs bundled tools such as ugrep from its own binary under another name, so the executable path must not be used. The sleep inhibitor counts only as a direct child. The desktop launcher runs with --bg-pty-host and is excluded, so the session reported is its child on a real tty.
